alt: Six-step diagram of the kidney transplant pathway from kidney failure planning to lifelong follow-up, with the nurse's role under each step.
Three-panel card: cPRA as the estimated share of donors with unacceptable antigens, donor-specific antibody against this donor's HLA, and the crossmatch testing reactivity against donor cells.
Reference card with four warning signs of pressure on a living donor and the action to take when a concern is found.
Flowchart for a safe organ offer call with channel verification, two-identifier check, readiness assessment, team instructions, read-back and documentation.
Illustration of a transplanted kidney's arterial, venous and ureteric connections with callouts for thrombosis, bleeding, urine leak, catheter blockage and lymphocele.
Concentration-time curve for twice-daily tacrolimus showing peaks after each dose and troughs just before the next, with correct and incorrect sampling times marked.
Flowchart for a rising creatinine after kidney transplant, grouping clues for volume, drug levels, rejection, infection, obstruction and vascular causes before an SBAR call.
Timeline of infection risk after kidney transplant from surgical infections in the first month to opportunistic infections in months one to six and community infections later.
Reference card of the five parts of a kidney transplant discharge plan, each with a teach-back check.
Diagram of three PhilHealth coverage pathways for kidney transplant: the procedure package and separate post-transplant packages for children and adults, with the registry requirement from May 2026.
Diagram of a closed-loop result measure, a Plan-Do-Study-Act cycle and a run chart with a balancing measure.
Diagram of the three separate records in the course: self-study completion, simulation pass and facility competency, each with its owner.

Line chart of the relative risk of death after kidney transplant compared with staying on the waiting list, peaking near 2.8 in the first two weeks, crossing 1.0 within months, and falling to about 0.32 by 18 months.

Bar chart showing 10-year graft survival of 63 percent when recipients had been on dialysis less than 6 months versus 29 percent after more than 2 years, using paired kidneys from the same donor, with adjusted registry figures of 69 versus 39 percent.
Team map with recipient-side roles, shared services and donor-side roles separated by firewalls, an allocation authority above them, and the nurse's task under each role.
Clothed patient figure surrounded by evaluation domains for kidney transplant candidates — infection, heart, cancer, psychosocial support and age — each with its KDIGO 2020 recommendation grade.

Four-step diagram: a transfusion, pregnancy or prior transplant triggers B cells to make HLA antibodies, cPRA rises, and the nurse notifies the laboratory; an old serum sample misses the antibody that a fresh sample detects.
Diagram explaining that blood group O candidates and highly sensitized candidates wait longer, with a paired exchange in which two incompatible donor–recipient pairs swap donors.
Before-and-after illustration of a living donor's kidneys: after donation the remaining kidney enlarges and each nephron filters more, so total kidney function settles near 70 percent of baseline.
Bar chart of lifetime kidney failure risk: 14 per 10,000 healthy nondonors, 90 per 10,000 living donors and 326 per 10,000 in the general population, with 15-year risks of 3.9 and 30.8 per 10,000.
Diagram of living donor selection: a GFR scale with bands below 60, 60 to 89 and 90 or more, and donor characteristics combined into a lifetime risk estimate compared with a program threshold.

ICU scene beside a five-row cascade showing what fails after brain death — catecholamine surge, loss of vessel tone, diabetes insipidus, low temperature and inflammation — and why each threatens the donor kidneys.

Three-step illustration of cold ischemia and reperfusion injury in a kidney tubular cell leading to delayed graft function, with static cold storage (26 percent delayed graft function) compared with machine perfusion (21 percent).

Balance diagram of donor factors linked to slower kidney start and shorter expected kidney life, with a decision card comparing an older candidate who may benefit from a kidney now and a younger candidate who may wait.

Timeline of induction immunosuppression around kidney transplant surgery: basiliximab for standard risk or anti-thymocyte globulin for high risk, a steroid pulse, and maintenance drugs building up, with nursing watch points for infusion reactions.
Graft anatomy sorted into before-, in- and after-the-kidney zones beside a five-step bedside checklist for falling urine output after transplant, ending in red escalation triggers.
Nephron diagram surrounded by six laboratory tiles showing why potassium may rise or fall, magnesium and phosphate fall, and calcium and glucose rise in the first week after kidney transplant.

Illustration of T-cell activation by three signals — donor HLA recognition through calcineurin, costimulation through CD28 and IL-2 signaling through mTOR — with each immunosuppressive drug class shown blocking its target.

Therapeutic window band for tacrolimus with rejection below and toxicity above, and a body map of its side effects including afferent arteriole narrowing in the kidney, high potassium, low magnesium, tremor, high blood pressure and new diabetes.

Gut wall and liver illustration of CYP3A enzymes and P-glycoprotein handling tacrolimus, beside a gauge showing drugs and foods that raise levels, such as fluconazole and pomelo, and those that lower levels, such as rifampicin.
Chart of five weeks of tacrolimus trough levels, each annotated: a reliable baseline, a falsely high peak drawn after the dose, a high level during diarrhea, and a low level after a generic switch.

Side-by-side comparison of T-cell-mediated rejection, with T cells invading tubules, and antibody-mediated rejection, with donor-specific antibodies inflaming small vessels and C4d staining, each with its biopsy appearance and treatment.

Magnified glomerular capillary wall showing its three layers holding back albumin, a damaged section leaking protein, and three common causes of proteinuria after kidney transplant with sampling tips.
Supine patient undergoing ultrasound-guided biopsy of a transplant kidney in the right lower abdomen, with an ultrasound inset, before-and-after nursing checklists and pooled complication rates.
Four-row card comparing the usual signs of infection with the quieter signs seen after kidney transplant, beside a stack of factors that make up the net state of immunosuppression.
Serostatus matrix showing CMV risk highest in donor-positive, recipient-negative recipients, beside cards comparing universal prophylaxis and preemptive monitoring, and the letermovir trial result.

BK polyomavirus progression from urine to blood to graft nephropathy without symptoms, a screening calendar of monthly blood tests to month 9 then every 3 months to 2 years, and thresholds for reducing immunosuppression.

Clothed transplant recipient surrounded by five long-term risk zones — heart disease, post-transplant diabetes, skin and other cancers, bone loss and chronic graft injury — with their drivers and screening points.

Tapering follow-up timeline from daily creatinine in week one to every two to three months after the first year, above a four-step loop for every result: received, reviewed, action documented and patient told.

Stylized Philippine map showing a recipient's home and local laboratory on an island, results sent through an approved channel to the transplant center, and the reviewed result returning to the patient, with tips on refills and travel.
Swimlane diagram of a six-step PhilHealth kidney transplant benefits workflow across the nurse, benefits staff and registry user, with a reminder that clinical candidacy is not benefit eligibility.
Reference card of the three Data Privacy Act principles for health data, role-based access for registry, claims and donor records, and approved versus unapproved channels for sharing.
Loop diagram from a bedside event to source document, registry entry, program report and policy, beside two versions of a report showing zero versus two graft losses when events go unrecorded.

Diagram of a quality measure as a fraction — abnormal results reviewed within 24 hours over all results meeting a prespecified threshold — with exclusions, three rules for trustworthy measurement and a note that review time is a surrogate.

Three-column just-culture diagram: human error leads to fixing the system and supporting the person, at-risk behavior to coaching, and rare reckless behavior to accountability, with weak and useful incident review answers.
Three cards for adolescents and young adults, frail older adults and pregnancy after kidney transplant, each with key outcome data and the nursing focus.
Circular track of four simulation stations — evaluation and donor, offer to recovery, discharge and triage, and Philippine workflow — with timing and the key trap at each stop.
Scoring card for the capstone simulation: five behaviors per station scored 2, 1 or 0, with pass requiring at least 32 of 40, at least 7 of 10 on every station and no critical error.

Career map with a foundation of PRC registration rising to four transplant nursing roles — ward transplant nurse, recipient coordinator, living donor coordinator and deceased donation coordinator — and the three steps for working abroad.
